ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r4.claim: After Abraham left the unbelievers and their land, God gave him prophetic children and the holy land; Isaac and Jacob consoled and strengthened him. Isaac was younger than Ishmael; Hagar's pregnancy provoked Sarah's jealousy before Sarah conceived Isaac.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p272/r4.anchor: ولما فارق الكفار وأرضهم أبدله منهم أولادا أنبياء، والأرض المقدسة

BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r3.claim: The sheikh says Abraham emigrated from Kutha to the Holy Land; God then gave him Isaac and Isaac’s son Jacob, not immediately upon departure, since the nearby promised child was Ishmael.
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r3.anchor: قال في "تفسير الشيخ" : فارتحل من كوثي إلى الأرض المقدسة

BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r4.claim: Isaac and Jacob are singled out as the prophetic lineage, or because Ishmael’s merit will be discussed separately; every one of them was made a prophet.
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r4.anchor: ولعل تخصيصهما بالذكر لأنهما شجرة الأنبياء

BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r5.claim: Kullan is placed first as the direct object for emphasis: every one of them, not only some, was made a prophet.
BURSEVI:v5p259#2/r5.anchor: كل واحد منهم جعلناه نبيا لا بعضهم دون بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r1.claim: After Abraham migrated away from his father and people, God gave him Isaac and Jacob in place of the family he left, though the births did not immediately follow the migration.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r1.anchor: بدل بن فارقهم من أبيه وقومه الكفره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r2.claim: The better-known chronology has Ishmael first, after Abraham's prayer for a righteous child; Hagar came, Sarah became jealous, then Isaac was born and later Jacob.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r2.anchor: والمشهور أن أول ما وهب له عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r3.claim: The order of the gift highlights how great God's compensation was for leaving kin: Isaac and Jacob became ancestors of many eminent prophets and descendants; Ishmael is then singled out for his own merit.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r3.anchor: ولعل ترتيب هبتهما على اعتزاله ههنا لبيان كمال عظم النعم التى اعطاها الله تعالى اياه بمقابله من اعتزالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r4.claim: The nearer account says Abraham first went to Harran, married Sarah, and had Isaac, from whom Jacob was born.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r4.anchor: وروى أنه عليه السلام لما قصد الشام اتى اولا حران وتزوج سارة وولدت له إسحاق وولد لاسحق يعقوب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r5.claim: “Each” can mean Isaac and Jacob, the two of them together, or the pair plus Abraham; the first is most natural, and the fronted object restricts the claim to each one rather than only some.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p102#3/r5.anchor: أي كل واحد من إسحاق ويعقوب أو منهما

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r11.claim: God's gift of Isaac and Jacob compensated Abraham for leaving his father and people so he would not feel lonely.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r11.anchor: كان ذلك كان عوضا عمن اعتزل من أبيه وقومه لئلا يضيق صدره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r12.claim: A mystical analogy says that when the Prophet withdrew from the whole cosmos, God compensated him with the pledge that those pledging to him were pledging to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p145/r12.anchor: ولما اعتزل نبينا ( صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ) الكون اجمع ما زاغ البصر وما طغى عوض عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r13.claim: After Abraham emigrated away from them and their gods, God gave him Isaac and Jacob, easing his loneliness and comforting him with children dear to God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r13.anchor: {وهبنا له} بعد الهجرة {إسحاق ويعقوب} آنسنا وحشته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p235/r14.claim: Both Isaac and Jacob were made prophets.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r2.claim: After Abraham migrated to Syria, God gave him Isaac and Jacob in place of the unbelievers he left. It is said he first reached Harran and married Sarah; the two may be singled out as prophetic lineages, while Ishmael is mentioned separately.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r2.anchor: { وهبنا له إسحق ويعقوب } بدل من فارقهم من الكفرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:48-49/r3.claim: “Both” refers either to Isaac and Jacob or to the sons collectively.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r7.claim: After Abraham migrated to the Holy Land and separated from idolaters, God gave him Isaac through his barren, postmenopausal wife.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r7.anchor: ولدا له لصلبه من زوجته العاقر العقيم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r8.claim: Isaac's son Jacob is singled out because they remained in Abraham's place and succeeded him there; God personally raised Ishmael after moving him as an infant to the Sacred Mosque.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r9.claim: God made Isaac and Jacob prophets of high rank, just as He had made Abraham a prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p538/r9.anchor: أي منهما { جعلنا نبيا * } عالي المقدار

QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r8.claim: After despairing of his father, Abraham was consoled by pious descendants granted prophethood and enduring good remembrance.
QUSHAYRI:v2p242/r8.anchor: لما أيس من أصله آنسه الله بما أكرمه من نسله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r1.claim: The text omits the completed separation after stating Abraham’s resolve, then names God’s reward: descendants who would comfort him in his loneliness, Isaac and Jacob, both prophets.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r1.anchor: طوي ذكر اعتزاله إياهم بعد أن ذكر عزمه عليه إيجازا في الكلام للعلم بأن مثله لا يعزم أمرا إلا نفذ عزمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r2.claim: The reward was not limited to Isaac and Jacob; Abraham also received Ishmael, and all three gifts followed his departure from his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r2.anchor: وليس مجازاة الله إبراهيم مقصورة على أن وهبه إسحاق ويعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r3.claim: Isaac and Jacob are named because Sarah also left her people, so the two were a shared gift and close companions matching Abraham’s sacrifice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r3.anchor: أن وهب لهما إسحاق وبعده يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r4.claim: Ishmael lived far away in Mecca to neighbor the House of God, a greater proximity than living with his father and brother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r4.anchor: أما إسماعيل فقد أراد الله أن يكون بعيدا عن إبراهيم في مكة ليكون جار بيت الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r5.claim: Ishmael receives separate mention in 38:48; Ibn ʿĀshūr also identifies the gentle boy promised after Abraham’s migration in 37:99–101 as Ishmael.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p123#2/r5.anchor: وقد خص إسماعيل بالذكر استقلالا عقب ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r13.claim: A report says Abraham left Kutha for Syria and, during the journey, met the ruler who gave Hajar to Sarah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r13.anchor: ويروى أنهم كانوا بأرض كوثا فرحل إبراهيم عليه السلام حتى نزل الشام وفي سفرته تلك لقي الجبار الذي أخدم هاجر بسارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r14.claim: When Abraham left his father's town and people, God compensated him with Isaac and Jacob, strengthening and consoling him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r14.anchor: إخبار من الله تعالى لمحمد عليه السلام أنه لما رحل عن بلد أبيه وقومه عوضه الله من ذلك ابنه إسحاق وابنه يعقوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r15.claim: A report says Isaac was younger than Ishmael, and Sarah became pregnant after Hajar conceived Ishmael and Sarah grew jealous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p19#2/r15.anchor: وإسحاق أصغر من إسماعيل، ولما حملت هاجر بإسماعيل غارت سارة فحملت ب إسحاق هذا فيما روي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r1.claim: Abraham migrated to Syria; God gave him Isaac and Jacob to console him for leaving his people with noble children.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r1.anchor: هاجر عنهم إلى ارض الشام فوهب الله له اسحاق ويعقوب فآنس الله وحشته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r2.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r2.claim: He says Isaac and Jacob were given after Ishmael.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r2.anchor: وإنما وهب له اسحاق ويعقوب بعد اسماعيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r3.claim: Kullan can refer to both Isaac and Jacob; Muqatil says it includes Abraham as well, with all three made prophets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p238#2/r3.anchor: وكلا أي وكلا من هذين وقال مقاتل وكلا يعني إبراهيم واسحاق ويعقوب

SULAMI:v1p428#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r1.claim: God recompenses spiritual leaders in proportion to their struggle, granting understanding of recitation in legal rulings and understanding of spiritual truth in afflictions.
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : عوض الأكابر على مقدار الحرب جعل فهم التلاوة للأحكام ، وجعل فهم الحقيقة للأسقام

SULAMI:v1p428#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r2.claim: Abraham's withdrawal brought Isaac and Jacob, Moses's withdrawal brought Aaron, and Muhammad's withdrawal from creation was paired with steadfast vision and exalted character; the source cites 19:53, 53:17, 68:4, and 48:10.
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r2.anchor: ولما اعتزل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم الأكوان أجمع ولم يزغ البصر في وقت النظرة وما طغى

SULAMI:v1p428#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r3.speaker: أبو محمد البلاذري
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r3.claim: Whoever gives up a worldly means for God's sake receives something better from Him in its place.
SULAMI:v1p428#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو محمد البلاذري : ما خر أحد على ربه في شيء من أسبابه وما ترك أحد له سببا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r1.claim: When Abraham separated from his father and people for God's sake, God replaced them with better company and granted him Isaac and Isaac's son Jacob.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r1.anchor: أبدله الله من هو خير منهم، ووهب له إسحاق ويعقوب، يعني ابنه وابن إسحاق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r2.claim: The Quran establishes Isaac as Jacob's father, and Abraham's descendants were prophets, bringing him joy during his lifetime.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r2.anchor: ولا خلاف أن إسحاق والد يعقوب، وهو نص القرآن في سورة البقرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r3.claim: Jacob must have become a prophet during Abraham's lifetime, since the passage names Jacob rather than his son Joseph, also a prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r3.anchor: فلو لم يكن يعقوب قد نبئ في حياة إبراهيم، لما اقتصر عليه، ولذكر ولده يوسف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r4.claim: A sound, agreed-upon report identifies Joseph as a prophet, son of the prophet Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham; another wording calls him the noble son of a noble lineage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p236#2/r4.anchor: فقال: "يوسف نبي الله، ابن يعقوب نبي الله، ابن إسحاق نبي الله

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r4.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r4.claim: Abraham separated from his people by migrating to the Holy Land.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r4.anchor: قيل: فارقهم إلى الأرض المقدسة، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r5.claim: God gave Abraham Isaac and grandson Jacob and made all three prophets to be followed in religion.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r5.anchor: وهبنا له أعطينا له إسحاق ويعقوب ابنا وابن ابن

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r13.claim: The phrase 'when he withdrew' supports using iʿtizāl for withdrawal from evil.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r13.anchor: اسم الاعتزال لا يرد إلا في الاعتزال عن الشر

JISHUMI:v6p4571/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r15.claim: When Abraham emigrated, God raised his rank; this is God's custom with His servants.
JISHUMI:v6p4571/r15.anchor: وتدل على أنه لما هاجر رفعه الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p24#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p24#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p24#2/r1.claim: Whoever leaves unbelieving, wicked people for God's sake loses nothing: God compensates him with believing prophetic children.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p24#2/r1.anchor: ما خسر على الله أحد ترك الكفار الفسقة لوجهه

MUQATIL:19:49-50/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:49-50/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:49-50/r1.claim: After Ibrahim left his people and their idols and migrated to the Holy Land, God granted him Isaac and Jacob; Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob were all prophets.
MUQATIL:19:49-50/r1.anchor: بعد الهجرة إلى الأرض المقدسة، { إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا } [آية: 49]، يعني إبراهيم، وإسحاق، ويعقوب.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r1.claim: After Abraham left the unbelievers and their idols, God gave him Isaac and Jacob; Jacob was an additional gift to provide companionship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r1.anchor: ولما اعتزل الكفار ومعبودهم ﴿ وهبنا له إسحاق ﴾ ولدا ﴿ ويعقوب ﴾ نافلة ليستأنس بهما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r2.claim: Both sons were made prophets; God compensated Abraham for leaving wicked unbelievers with believing prophetic children.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p39#4/r2.anchor: كل واحد منهما ﴿ جعلنا نبيا ﴾ أي لما ترك الكفار الفجار لوجهه عوضه أولادا مؤمنين أنبياء

QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the gift of Isaac and Jacob comforted Abraham's loneliness through children.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:47-50/r16.anchor: أي آنسنا وحشته بولد عن ابن عباس وغيره.

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r1.claim: Abraham’s religious and physical separation and migration did not cost him in religion or worldly life; God compensated him with prophetic sons.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r1.anchor: لما اعتزلهم في دينهم وفي بلدهم واختار الهجرة إلى ربه إلى حيث أمره لم يضره ذلك دينا ودنيا

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r2.claim: Being made a messenger whom people must obey is among the highest worldly and afterlife blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r2.anchor: ولا حالة في الدين والدنيا للبشر أرفع من أن يجعل الله له رسولا إلى خلقه ويلزم الخلق طاعته

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r6.claim: Because Abraham separated from people and their idols, God blessed his descendants with Isaac and Jacob, both prophets.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r6.anchor: إن الخليل اعتزل عن الخلق على ما قال : { وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r7.claim: Because Abraham disavowed his father for God, God named him the father of the Muslims.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r7.anchor: أنه تبرأ من أبيه في الله تعالى على ما قال : { فلما تبين له أنه عدو لله تبرأ منه

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r8.claim: Because Abraham laid his son down to sacrifice him, God ransomed the son with a great sacrifice.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r8.anchor: تل ولده للجبين ليذبحه على ما قال : { فلما أسلما وتله للجبين

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r9.claim: Because Abraham surrendered himself to God, God made the fire cool and safe for him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r9.anchor: فجعل الله تعالى النار عليه بردا وسلاما

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r10.claim: Because Abraham cared for this community and prayed for a messenger among them, God included him in the blessings of the five daily prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r10.anchor: أشفق على هذه الأمة فقال : { ربنا وابعث فيهم رسولا منهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r11.claim: In the matter of Sarah, Abraham was described as faithful, and God made his footprint a blessed place of prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r11.anchor: في حق سارة في قوله : { وإبراهيم الذى وفى

RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r12.claim: Because Abraham opposed all creatures for God, God took him as an intimate friend, demonstrating that no one loses by serving God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p197/r12.anchor: عادى كل الخلق في الله فقال : { فإنهم عدو لى إلا رب العالمين

STUDYQURAN:19:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:49/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:49/r1.claim: Isaac and Jacob are elsewhere described as God's gifts to Abraham; other passages give variant glad tidings of descendants.
STUDYQURAN:19:49/r1.anchor: Isaac and Jacob are also described as gifts bestowed upon Abraham by God

STUDYQURAN:19:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:49/r2.speaker: Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:19:49/r2.claim: Each made a prophet includes Abraham as well as Isaac and Jacob; the two sons compensate him for losing his father and people, and are a better gift.
STUDYQURAN:19:49/r2.anchor: the gift of these two prophets was far better than what he had lost

TAB-FULL:v15p557/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p557/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p557/r1.claim: When Abraham separated from his people and their idols, God comforted his loneliness by replacing them with better people, more honored by God: Isaac and his grandson Jacob.
TAB-FULL:v15p557/r1.anchor: فلما اعتزل إبراهيم قومه وعبادة ما كانوا يعبدون من دون الله من الأوثان آنسنا وحشته من فراقهم، وأبدلناه منهم بمن هو خير منهم

TAB-FULL:v15p557/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p557/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p557/r2.claim: God made Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob all prophets; كُلّ is singular in wording, so the predicate is singular نبيا.
TAB-FULL:v15p557/r2.anchor: وقال تعالى ذكره: {وكلا جعلنا نبيا} [مريم: 49] فوحد، ولم يقل أنبياء، لتوحيد لفظ كل

TABATABAI:19:41-43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:41-43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:41-43/r1.claim: The passage sketches Abraham’s argument with his father against idols, his separation from the people and their gods, and God’s gifts of Isaac, Jacob, and an enduring good name for his descendants.
TABATABAI:19:41-43/r1.anchor: محاجته أباه في أمر الأصنام بما آتاه الله من الهدى الفطري والمعرفة اليقينية

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r7.claim: Isaac is named first to introduce the line of Israelite prophets, with Jacob following because many prophets came from his descendants; both were made prophets.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r7.anchor: لعل الاقتصار على ذكر إسحاق لتعلق الغرض بذكر توالي النبوة في الشجرة الإسرائيلية

TABATABAI:19:47-50/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r8.claim: The gift of mercy may refer to imamate, as in the cited account of Isaac and Jacob.
TABATABAI:19:47-50/r8.anchor: من الممكن أن يكون المراد به الإمامة كما وقع في قوله

TABRISI:19:49-50/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:49-50/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:49-50/r2.claim: After Ibrahim left them and migrated to the Holy Land, God granted him Isaac and grandson Jacob, both prophets.
TABRISI:19:49-50/r2.anchor: أي فارقهم وهاجرهم إلى الأرض المقدسة

TABRISI:19:49-50/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:49-50/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:49-50/r3.claim: God comforted Ibrahim's loneliness after separation with children honored by God and made prophets.
TABRISI:19:49-50/r3.anchor: أي أنسنا وحشته من فراقهم بأولاد كرام على الله

THALABI:v6p217/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p217/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p217/r9.claim: After Abraham left his people and their idols to migrate, God granted him Isaac and Jacob, and made Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob prophets.
THALABI:v6p217/r9.anchor: فذهب مهاجرا وهبنا له بعد الهجرة إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p261/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p261/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p261/r1.claim: Abraham emigrated away from them toward Syria; God comforted him for their loss by granting noble sons Isaac and Jacob, making each a prophet.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r5.claim: After Abraham left them and migrated to Syria, God gave him Isaac and Jacob and made each a prophet.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:47-50/r5.anchor: فلما اعتزلهم وما يعبدون من دون الله } وذهب مهاجرا إلى الشام { وهبنا له } بعد الهجرة { إسحق ويعقوب وكلا } منهما { جعلنا } ه { نبيا }.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r2.claim: The things Abraham left behind were his people's idols.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p228/r3.claim: The three made prophets are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r1.speaker: tefsirci ve tarihçiler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r1.claim: Commentators and historians say Abraham migrated through Harran, Palestine, Egypt, then back to Palestine with Sarah, Lot, and Lot's wife; Lot settled in Sodom and Gomorrah, while Abraham remained in Palestine.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r1.anchor: İbrâhim aleyhisselâm Allah yolunda hicret ederek önce Harran’a, sonra Filistin’e, buradan da Mısır’a gitmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r2.claim: God granted elderly Abraham and Sarah Isaac, then Isaac's son Jacob, making them prophets; later Israelite prophets descended from them, while Ishmael, Abraham's first son by Hagar, became ancestor of the Hijaz Arabs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:49/r2.anchor: Burada kendisi ve eşi Sâre yaşlanmış oldukları halde Allah onlara oğulları İshak’ı lutfetti

SAMIN-DURR:19:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:49/r1.claim: وكلا is a fronted first object, and نبيا is the second object of جعلنا.
SAMIN-DURR:19:49/r1.anchor: " وكلا " مفعول مقدم هو الأول، و " نبيا " هو الثاني.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophets' accounts show Christians that earlier prophets taught Muhammad's message, while warning Quraysh that Abraham's and Ishmael's religion differs from what they now follow; the Qur'an presents Abraham's true religion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The real religion of Abraham (sws) is the one which the Qur’ān is presenting before them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's declaration amounted to migration, and he left his people after proclaiming his disavowal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: tantamount to migration. Thus after this proclamation he migrated from them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The omission of Ishmael seems striking because he fathered the Ishmaelites, including Muhammad as God's final prophet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: to them belonged Muḥammad, the last and final prophet of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Naming Jacob with Isaac highlights three successive prophets—Abraham, his son, and grandson; adding Joseph shows a prophetic family unmatched in human history.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the father, the son and the grandson were all prophets.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Imām Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Farāhī argued that Ishmael was the greatest blessing granted through Abraham's migration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the greatest blessing of migration – as proven by my mentor Imām Farāhī in his book Fī man huwa al-dhabīḥ – was Ishmael (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi explains Ishmael's omission from this list by noting that he was already mentioned independently so the primarily addressed Arabian idolaters would focus on their ancestor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: In my opinion, the reason for this lack of mention is that he is mentioned ahead independently.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Zacharias' story prepares for Jesus, and Abraham's old-age childbearing provides another miraculous-birth example; therefore miraculous birth does not justify divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: examples of miraculous birth are exist before the times of Jesus (sws) too. Ascribing divinity to someone just because of this reason is mere foolishness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Farāhī's tract exposes distortions and interpolations and restores the histories of Abraham and the other celebrated figure discussed with him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: my mentor Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī has exposed all these distortions and interpolations and revived the history of both these celebrated personalities

BURHAN:v2p131/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p131/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p131/r9.claim: The saying that disbelief's head is East is linked to Abraham's vision: observing God's dominion entails trials, and guidance comes from God after disavowal.
